reading: Indiana University operates a purpose-built data center on its Bloomington campus, completed in 2009 at 90,000 square feet, with a sister facility at IUPUI in Indianapolis. The building was engineered as a stand-alone reinforced concrete structure designed to withstand the impact of an EF5 tornado, reflecting the Midwest's tornado risk profile, and is organized into access-controlled pods requiring both ID card and hand scan authentication. The Enterprise Pod houses academic and administrative systems supporting the university's operations, while the Research Pod houses supercomputing infrastructure, including the Big Red II and Karst systems, with more than 21,000 processing cores supporting faculty and student research computing across the university. The facility includes backup diesel generators rated at 2,200 horsepower each with 10,000 gallons of onsite fuel storage, maintains equipment at 70 degrees Fahrenheit, and runs a 24/7 operations center monitoring building and equipment performance, earning a Tier 3 rating from the Uptime Institute, a certification level uncommon among university-operated facilities and comparable to many commercial colocation sites. As with the University of Florida's HiPerGator program and the Alabama Supercomputer Authority elsewhere in this registry, Indiana University's data center exists to serve internal research and administrative computing needs rather than outside paying tenants.
